title: California AG Launches Probe Into Nvidia Over Ex-CEO's Alleged Chinese Spy Scandal
snippet: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia compromised advanced AI chip technology or misled investors following former CEO Jensen Huang's scandal involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.
content:
SAN FRANCISCO — California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a formal investigation into Nvidia Corp. after revelations surfaced regarding former CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive suspected of acting as a Chinese spy.

State prosecutors served an investigative subpoena on the Santa Clara-based chipmaker on Thursday. The probe centers on whether Nvidia's cutting-edge artificial intelligence hardware or confidential trade secrets were unlawfully transferred to China, and whether the tech giant violated state corporate securities laws by misleading shareholders and the public.

Broader National Security and Regulatory Fallout

State officials are examining whether Nvidia's public statements, press communications, or regulatory filings contained deceptive disclosures. Under California law, misleading investors carries stiff penalties.

The state investigation follows reports that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has launched its own inquiry into the company's financial disclosures. The controversy escalated last week with Huang's sudden resignation as chief executive following revelations about his affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean data center company that served as a key Nvidia customer. U.S. intelligence agencies suspect she has ties to the Chinese government.

Lobbying Impact and Political Tensions

The high-stakes probe comes as Washington tightens export restrictions on advanced semiconductors to curb Beijing's technological advancements. Huang had previously been an active presence in the nation's capital, leveraging connections within the Trump administration to push back against stringent export controls.

Bonta raised concerns about potential political leniency at the federal level given Huang's political access, stating he was not confident federal officials would take appropriate action. Nvidia has not yet publicly responded to inquiries regarding the state subpoena.
